AADHARHFC.method_1: Peer-relative EARNINGS multiple: 14-19x trailing FY26 EPS of Rs 24.77 (PAT Rs 1,095.88 cr / 44.24 cr shares) = Rs 347-471. The affordable-HFC peer group (Aavas, Home First, India Shelter) commands ~18-22x trailing; I applied a deliberate haircut for the Blackstone PE-sponsor sell-down overhang, an untested credit cycle in informal-income mortgages, and an ROE (15.75%) that is only middling despite 20% PAT growth. 14x is the bear case (growth decelerates to low-teens, credit cost normalises toward 0.6-0.8% of assets, derating to PNB Housing/Can Fin territory); 19x is the bull (sustains 18-20% growth and levers up to 18-19% ROE, retaining a Home First-like rating).
AADHARHFC.method_2: BALANCE-SHEET anchor: 10-year residual-income build off FY26 BVPS of Rs 170.45 (net worth Rs 7,540.89 cr). ROE path starts ~16.5%, rises to ~18-18.5% as the over-capitalised balance sheet levers from 3.63x toward ~4.5-5x assets/equity (ROA held ~4.0-4.3%), then fades to ~15-16%; terminal ROE 14.5-15.0%, terminal g 8% (India nominal GDP plus mortgage-penetration tailwind), CoE 12.0-13.5% (6.5% G-sec + ~1.1 beta on a ~6% India ERP). Clean-surplus book roll-forward with payout rising 5% to 35%. Output Rs 265-400/share, i.e. justified P/B 1.55-2.35x; central case (CoE 13.0%) lands at Rs 295 and CoE 12.5% at Rs 372 - the spread IS the honest uncertainty, since the terminal RI denominator (CoE - g) is only 4.0-5.5%.
AADHARHFC.methods_are_independent: Yes, and here they actually diverged - the RI leg's centre (~Rs 295-330) sat roughly 25% BELOW the multiple leg's centre (~Rs 405), forcing a reconciliation rather than confirming a number. The divergence mechanism is concrete: Aadhar is materially over-capitalised (equity/assets 27.5%, leverage just 3.63x vs 4.5-5.5x normal for an HFC), so reported ROE of 15.75% sits far below its ROA-implied potential (4.33% ROA x 5x leverage = ~21%). A trailing P/E is structurally blind to that - it prices the profit flow without asking how much equity was burned to produce it, and is set by peer-group sentiment. The RI leg is driven by precisely that gap: it discounts (ROE - CoE) x book over a fade path, so leverage policy, credit cost, terminal ROE and CoE move it hard while leaving a peer P/E untouched. Concretely, dropping CoE from 13.5% to 12.0% swings leg 2 by ~80% and leg 1 not at all; conversely a sector-wide derating would halve leg 1 and leave leg 2 unchanged. I deliberately did NOT use a cash-flow leg: for a lender, loan-book growth is an operating outflow, so OCF is structurally negative (-Rs 2,808 cr in FY26, -Rs 3,027 cr in FY25) and any FCF-yield construction would be meaningless, not independent. I also did not pair P/E with EV/EBITDA - for an NBFC that would be one method restated, and EV is undefined when borrowings are raw material rather than financing. Residual linkage acknowledged: both legs share the ROE identity, but ROE is not a constant here - it is exactly the variable the two legs treat differently.
AADHARHFC.rationale: Aadhar is an affordable-housing NBFC-HFC: FY26 revenue Rs 3,672.58 cr, PAT Rs 1,095.88 cr (+20% YoY, 26% 3-yr CAGR), net worth Rs 7,540.89 cr, total assets Rs 27,398.84 cr, with an excellent 4.33% ROA but only 15.75% ROE on average equity because the post-IPO balance sheet is heavily over-capitalised (equity/assets 27.5%, leverage 3.63x); PAT margin has improved steadily 26.7% to 29.8% and opex/revenue is stable at ~21.6%, so this is a genuinely well-run franchise, not a levered mirage. Leg 1 (earnings multiple, 14-19x trailing EPS of Rs 24.77) gives Rs 347-471. Leg 2 (residual income off BVPS Rs 170.45, ROE fading 16.5% up to ~18% then back to ~15%, terminal g 8%, CoE 12.0-13.5%) gives Rs 265-400, i.e. justified P/B 1.55-2.35x. The legs did not overlap at their centres - the RI leg charges the company for the excess equity the P/E ignores - so I took the overlap zone (Rs 347-400) and widened it for genuine CoE uncertainty to Rs 330-430, roughly 13-17x trailing earnings and 1.9-2.5x book. At Rs 496.70 (Rs 21,974 cr mcap, 20.1x trailing, 2.91x book) the market is implicitly underwriting ~21-22% perpetual ROE on 8% growth from a business currently earning 15.75%, requiring simultaneous leverage-up, zero ROA compression and no credit cycle; that is a good franchise at a full price, ~15% above my band top - REDUCE, not AVOID.

ACE.method_1: Normalised mid-cycle earnings multiple: normalised revenue ~3,400 cr at a 14.5% EBITDA margin (between FY23's 10.4% trough and FY26's 15.4% peak) gives EBITDA ~493, EBIT ~455, NOPAT ~340 cr at a 25.4% tax rate. Applied 22-30x for a dominant-share (60%+ pick-n-carry crane) niche franchise with 30%+ core ROCE, discounted from boom-cycle Indian cap-goods multiples because growth has just stalled. Treasury added separately at ~950 cr (haircut from the 1,391 cr of cash plus non-current investments). Range Rs 720-960/sh.
ACE.method_2: Sustainable free-cash-flow yield: normalised OCF ~420 cr (the FY24-FY26 plateau of 412-433) less sustaining capex of 80-140 cr (D&A is only 35 but gross block has doubled and 4-yr average capex is 141) gives owner FCF of 280-340 cr. Capitalised at a 3.75-4.75% demanded yield for a cyclical mid-cap capital-goods name with net cash gives operating EV 6,100-8,800 cr; add ~950 cr treasury. Range Rs 592-819/sh.
ACE.methods_are_independent: The legs disagree because ACE's accounting profit and its cash generation have decoupled over the last three years, and only one leg can see it. PAT rose 328 -> 409 -> 415 while OCF was dead flat at 433 -> 412 -> 417, and capex ran at roughly 4x depreciation (175, 221, 93 vs D&A of 23-35). The earnings leg capitalises reported profit and is structurally blind to how much capital the business consumes to produce it; the cash leg charges that capital and therefore lands ~20% lower at the midpoint. They would converge only if capex normalised to D&A and working capital stopped absorbing growth - i.e. the disagreement is exactly the open question about this business, not an artefact. The direction of divergence is informative too: if the capex ramp is genuine growth investment (new agri/crane capacity) the FCF leg under-values, which is why I did not simply take the lower leg. A third, fully independent balance-sheet check corroborated the cash leg rather than the earnings leg: justified P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) with ROE 20.6%, CoE 11.5-12% and g 8-9% gives 3.2-4.6x against an actual 6.3x, implying Rs 676-761.
ACE.rationale: Earnings leg: normalised NOPAT ~340 cr (revenue 3,400 at 14.5% EBITDA) at 22-30x plus ~950 cr treasury = Rs 720-960; cash leg: normalised FCF 280-340 cr (OCF ~420 less sustaining capex 80-140) at a 3.75-4.75% yield plus treasury = Rs 592-819; intersection Rs 700-880. Key figures: price 1,070.30 on 11.9 cr shares = 12,736 cr mcap, net cash 643 (total treasury including non-current investments ~1,391), net worth 2,011 (P/B 6.3x), FY26 revenue 3,280 (-1.4%), EBITDA 504 (15.4%), PAT 415 (+1.4%), ROE 20.6%. This is a genuinely high-return franchise - dominant in pick-n-carry cranes, core operating capital employed of only ~635 cr ex-treasury - but FY26 is the first flat year after a 54% two-year revenue run, consistent with a CEV Stage-V pre-buy air-pocket landing on top of a cyclical plateau, and margins are at the top of their range rather than the bottom. At 1,070 the market is paying 34.7x normalised NOPAT, 23.9x normalised EBITDA and accepting a 2.6% FCF yield for zero current growth, roughly 22% above the top of my band, while the justified-P/B cross-check independently points below my band rather than above it. I call REDUCE rather than AVOID because the balance sheet is pristine, the franchise is real, and one flat year in a cyclical does not break the thesis - a FY27 re-acceleration could vindicate the price - but at this multiple the burden of proof sits with the bull.

AIIL.method_1: Justified P/B on sustainable ROE. FY26 stated net worth Rs 14,727.84 cr over ~84.92 cr shares = BVPS ~Rs 173.4. Sustainable ROE 14-17% (FY26 actual 13.1%; FY24-25's 41-125% were bull-market marks off a far smaller base), CoE 14.5-16% (concentrated illiquid prop book, key-person dependence, no contractual earnings), g 8-10%. (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) spans ~0.75x-1.55x; widened to 0.9x-1.8x to credit probable conservatism in the carrying value of the acquired RCFL/RHFL distressed books and a genuine manager premium. Range: Rs 156-312/sh.
AIIL.method_2: Capitalised realised free cash. Four-year OCF 244.69 + 3,279.16 + 325.72 + 1,524.49 = Rs 5,374 cr, avg Rs 1,343 cr/yr; four-year capex avg Rs 80 cr/yr; normalised free cash ~Rs 1,263 cr = Rs 14.87/sh. Capitalised at 11x-18x (growth-adjusted perpetuity for a reinvesting but volatile, non-contractual, key-person cash stream at r~15%, g 6-9%). Range: Rs 164-268/sh. Caveat stated plainly: for an investment company OCF absorbs net securities purchases/sales, so single years swing on net buyer/seller posture; four-year averaging mitigates it, and FY26's own OCF of Rs 1,524 cr sits near the average.
AIIL.methods_are_independent: Yes, and for this company the gap between them is the whole question. Leg 1 takes accounting book (a mark on an unobserved portfolio) and asks what return on equity vs cost of equity justifies paying a multiple of it; book value never enters Leg 2. Leg 2 takes cash actually harvested through the cash flow statement and capitalises it; ROE, CoE and book never enter Leg 1's inputs. They diverge exactly when marks run ahead of realisations — which is empirically what happened here: cumulative FY23-26 reported PAT of Rs 14,759 cr against cumulative OCF of only Rs 5,374 cr (~36% conversion), and FY26 book growth of 0.3% despite Rs 1,929 cr of reported PAT. Had cash conversion matched the headline marks, Leg 2 would have landed near Rs 700+/sh; had FY24's Rs 3,279 cr OCF been representative, far higher again; instead it lands below Leg 1's midpoint. Deliberately avoided the P/E-vs-EV/EBITDA trap, which is doubly meaningless here since "revenue" and "EBITDA" for a prop investment book are just fair-value gains relabelled.
AIIL.rationale: Authum is a listed proprietary investment company/NBFC: FY26 investments Rs 15,841 cr of Rs 19,211 cr total assets, borrowings Rs 3,631 cr against net worth Rs 14,728 cr (0.25x leverage), so book approximates marked NAV and EV multiples are meaningless. CRITICAL DATA FLAG: the API's shares field (31.32 cr) is an unrestated weighted average spanning a 4:1 bonus during FY26 — BS share capital went 16.98 to 84.92 cr (exactly 5.00x) with net worth flat, confirming a reserve capitalisation, and the vendor's own peer-map P/B of 3.29 at Rs 561 independently implies ~86 cr shares; I used 84.92 cr, giving market cap Rs 45,798 cr, BVPS Rs 173, P/B 3.11x and restated P/E 23.7x — not the 1.15x/8.8x the stale count implies, so any engine using 31.32 cr will overstate per-share intrinsic by ~2.7x. Leg 1 (justified P/B, ROE 14-17%, CoE 14.5-16%, g 8-10%) gives 0.9-1.8x book = Rs 156-312; Leg 2 (normalised free cash Rs 1,263 cr at 11-18x) gives Rs 164-268. The decisive evidence is that FY26 book rose 0.3% despite Rs 1,929 cr of reported PAT — roughly Rs 1,890 cr leaked below the P&L through fair-value/OCI — so the economic comprehensive return was near zero and the FY24-25 ROEs cannot recur off a Rs 14,700 cr base. I would defend Rs 175-310 (the top already pays ~1.8x book); at Rs 539 the market demands ~25% sustainable ROE in perpetuity from a no-moat, key-person prop book yielding 2.8% on free cash and paying a Rs 2.13 cr dividend, hence AVOID — a valuation call, not a timing one, given the stock has run 185 to 539 in 27 months. Disclosure: the vendor blob carried a third-party analyst tag "Bullish"; that is IndianAPI consensus sentiment, not the engine's verdict, intrinsic value or MoS, none of which I retrieved or saw.

APTUS.method_1: Residual-income / justified-P/B balance-sheet anchor. FY26 net worth Rs 5,060 cr (Rs 101.1/sh), CoE 13.5% (Rf ~6.75%, ERP ~6%, beta ~1.1), explicit ~10-year excess-return phase at ~20% ROE with 76% retention (book compounds ~15%/yr, B10 ~Rs 20,800 cr), terminal fade to 16.5% ROE at g 8.5% (terminal P/B 1.60x). Base value Rs 233/sh; bear (7-yr runway, 18% ROE, CoE 14.5%, terminal ROE 15%, g 8%) Rs 130; bull (12-yr runway, 22% ROE, CoE 12.5%, terminal P/B 2.0x) Rs 385. Defensible sub-range Rs 190-280, i.e. 1.9-2.8x current book, centre ~Rs 235.
APTUS.method_2: Trailing earnings multiple on reported FY26 EPS of Rs 18.84 (PAT Rs 942.94 cr / 50.05 cr shares) at 12-16x. Multiple set from business character, not from the market quote: upper-middle band for a fully-secured lender compounding PAT 23% with 20% ROE, ~14% cost-to-income and ~0.5% implied credit cost; discounted from a top-tier franchise multiple for four-state South-India concentration, self-employed/informal borrower base, and competition plus regulatory attention on 17-18% asset yields. Range Rs 226-301, centre ~Rs 264 (implied 2.2-3.0x book).
APTUS.methods_are_independent: Yes, and they do in fact disagree. Leg 1 is anchored on the Rs 5,060 cr book and is driven by cost of equity, the LENGTH of the excess-return runway and the terminal ROE fade — it never asks what anyone pays for earnings. Leg 2 is driven by realised earnings power and a franchise multiple, and makes no CoE, retention or terminal-fade assumption at all. Critically I do NOT reuse one ROE across both, which is what would collapse them into the P/E = P/B / ROE identity: leg 1 runs on a faded terminal ROE of 15-18% plus an explicit discount rate, leg 2 on no ROE input whatsoever. They can and do diverge: base centres are Rs 235 vs Rs 264 (12% apart) and the full input spans are Rs 130-385 vs Rs 226-301. Mechanically, if ROE mean-reverts to 15% the balance-sheet leg collapses (terminal P/B goes to ~1.1x) while a trailing-earnings leg barely moves for a year or two; conversely if leverage builds from 2.58x toward 4x, EPS and the earnings leg rise sharply while the book anchor is unchanged. No cash-flow leg was used and none is possible: operating cash flow is negative in all four years (-Rs 489 cr in FY26) purely because loan-book growth is classified as operating, and net_debt is null, so FCF yield and EV multiples are meaningless for this entity.
APTUS.rationale: Aptus is an affordable housing financier: FY26 total income Rs 2,192 cr (+25%), PAT Rs 943 cr (+26%, 3-yr CAGR 23.3%), net worth Rs 5,060 cr, ROE 20.1% on average equity and ROA ~7.8% — genuinely elite, though the ROA is flattered by very low leverage (assets/equity 2.58x, D/E 1.56x vs 4-5x for peer HFCs), with ~12.7% NIM, ~14% cost-to-income and only ~Rs 63 cr of implied credit cost. Leg 1, a residual-income/justified-P/B anchor off the Rs 5,060 cr book at CoE 13.5% with a ~10-year 20%-ROE excess-return runway fading to 16.5% ROE at 8.5% growth, gives Rs 190-280 (1.9-2.8x book), centre ~Rs 235. Leg 2, 12-16x trailing FY26 EPS of Rs 18.84 — upper-middle for a 20%-ROE, 23%-growth secured lender, marked down for South-India concentration, informal-income borrowers and yield compression risk — gives Rs 226-301, centre ~Rs 264. No cash-flow leg exists here: OCF is negative every year because disbursements sit in operating, and net debt is undefined for a lender. Intersecting the two, I would defend Rs 215-285 (2.1-2.8x book, 11-15x trailing earnings); at Rs 261.20 the stock sits inside the band and modestly above my ~Rs 250 centre, so HOLD — the quality and the leverage runway are real, but the price already pays for them, and the dataset carries no GNPA/CRAR/AUM disclosure (all nulls), which is why I will not tighten the band further.

ASKAUTOLTD.method_1: Normalised-earnings multiple: 22-27x P/E on normalised EPS of Rs 14.0-16.0 (trailing FY26 EPS 15.08; low end normalises EBITDA margin back to 12.0% from a peak 12.8%, high end rolls forward on capacity already installed). Gives Rs 310-430.
ASKAUTOLTD.method_2: Two-stage FCFF DCF with an explicit reinvestment charge: NOPAT 319.5 (EBIT 419.8 x 76.1%), reinvestment rate set as g/incremental-ROIC using the measured incremental ROIC of 18.5%, stage-1 growth 14-18% for 5 years fading to 5.0-5.5% terminal, WACC 10.5-12.0%. EV 5,459-7,123 less net debt 665 gives Rs 200-330.
ASKAUTOLTD.methods_are_independent: They can and do diverge because one charges reinvestment and the other does not. The P/E leg values accounting earnings and takes no view on the capital needed to sustain them; the DCF leg subtracts net capex and working-capital build from NOPAT before discounting. For ASK that difference is enormous rather than cosmetic: FY26 capex of 484 is 4.2x depreciation of 114, working capital absorbed ~110 cr (receivables 195->302, inventory 232->324), and cumulative FY23-26 FCF is MINUS 166 cr against cumulative PAT of 841 cr. A P/E leg is blind to all of that; the DCF leg is driven by it. The legs in fact disagree materially - Rs 310-430 vs Rs 200-330, roughly a 50% gap at the midpoints, overlapping only in a narrow Rs 310-330 window - which is the opposite of the mechanical agreement you get from pairing P/E with EV/EBITDA off the same year. Note I deliberately did NOT use EV/EBITDA as a leg, since at a fixed 24% tax rate and known D&A/interest it is just the PAT multiple restated.
ASKAUTOLTD.rationale: Earnings-multiple leg gives Rs 310-430 (22-27x normalised EPS 14.0-16.0); reinvestment-charged FCFF DCF gives Rs 200-330 (incremental ROIC 18.5%, 14-18% stage-1 growth, 10.5-12.0% WACC, net debt 665). Key figures: revenue 2,555->4,176 over FY23-26 (18% CAGR) with EBITDA margin expanding 9.3%->12.8% and PAT 123->297 (34% CAGR), ROE ~25%, but FY26 capex 484 at 4.2x depreciation and cumulative four-year FCF of MINUS 166 cr, with borrowings up 412->679 in a single year. This is a genuinely value-creating market leader in 2W braking and aluminium lightweighting whose P&L quality is not matched by cash conversion - every rupee of growth so far has been debt- and reinvestment-funded, and asset turns have fallen 3.14x to 2.73x as the new block comes on. I settle at Rs 275-400, above the pure intersection because the DCF double-penalises a mid-ramp where ~380 cr of new gross block is not yet productive, and below the multiple leg's top because 27x cannot be defended on zero free cash flow and rising leverage. At Rs 528 the market pays 35x earnings, 20.7x EV/EBITDA and 7.9x book - a full franchise multiple for a capital-hungry auto ancillary - which is ~32% above my upper bound, hence REDUCE rather than AVOID: good business, wrong price.

AZAD.method_1: Normalised (ramp-adjusted) earnings multiple. The existing Rs 1,036 cr net fixed-asset block, at Azad's own demonstrated mature asset turn of 1.13x (FY24 revenue 340.8 on net FA 302.7), supports ~Rs 1,100-1,200 cr of revenue. At a 36-38% EBITDA margin that is EBITDA 400-450, less D&A stepped up to ~95 (FY26 dep of 52.8 on a block added late in the year is understated), less ~30 net interest on Rs 474 cr borrowings against Rs 191 cr cash, taxed at 28% gives normalised PAT of Rs 175-215 cr, reachable FY28-29. Multiple: 20-30x, not the 40-60x Indian precision/defence peers fetch, because a firm needing reinvestment of g/ROIC (25/13 = ~190% of NOPAT) to grow cannot support a franchise multiple. Discounting ~2 years at 12%: equity Rs 3,500-6,450 cr, i.e. Rs 540-995/share, central ~Rs 600.
AZAD.method_2: Capital/returns (balance-sheet) anchor via EV/IC = (ROIC - g)/(WACC - g). Invested capital today = net worth 1,528.9 + net debt 283.5 = Rs 1,812 cr. Mature-state IC ~Rs 1,850-2,000 cr (net FA ~1,036 maintained + working capital at 70-80% of a Rs 1,140 cr revenue base, versus 62-86% actually run FY24-26). Mature EBIT at 28-31% margin = 320-353, NOPAT 230-255, so ROIC = 12-14% against a WACC of ~12% (Rf 6.8%, ERP 6%, beta ~1.0-1.1, small debt weight). At g = 8% that puts EV/IC at 1.0-1.75x, EV Rs 1,812-3,170 cr, equity Rs 1,530-2,890 cr = Rs 236-445/share. A deliberately generous variant (asset turn 1.3x, EBITDA margin 40%, working capital cut to 55% of sales, ROIC 17.6%) reaches ~Rs 630/share and is my effective ceiling from this leg.
AZAD.methods_are_independent: They can and do diverge violently here, which is the point. Leg 1 values accounting earnings and is completely agnostic about how much capital produced them: it would return the identical answer for a company with the same PAT and half the balance sheet. Leg 2 values the capital and the return it earns and is agnostic about the earnings multiple: it would return roughly the same answer even if PAT doubled, provided invested capital doubled alongside it. Neither is a restatement of the other, unlike P/E and EV/EBITDA on a common year, which are locked together by interest, D&A and tax. Applied to Azad they disagreed by 3-4x on first pass — franchise multiples on leg 1 implied Rs 810-1,490 while leg 2 implied Rs 250-450 — and the disagreement was informative rather than noise: it revealed that the earnings multiple I was carrying (35-50x) was inconsistent with a 12-14% ROIC against a 12% WACC, forcing leg 1's multiple down to 20-30x. The reconciled overlap, roughly Rs 350-700, is where the two legs can both be defended. Independent corroboration also comes from the cash statement, which neither leg uses directly: cumulative FY23-26 operating cash flow of minus Rs 83 cr against cumulative PAT of Rs 287 cr is the same story leg 2 tells in balance-sheet form.
AZAD.rationale: Azad is a genuine precision-engineering franchise - turbine airfoils and blades for GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and MHI, with multi-year qualification barriers - compounding revenue at 33% (FY23 252 to FY26 603) on a 37% EBITDA margin, but it is a capital sponge: FY23-26 capex of Rs 1,027 cr against cumulative operating cash flow of MINUS Rs 83 cr, with working capital now at 86% of sales (receivables 312 + inventory 329 - payables 85). Leg 1, normalised earnings: the Rs 1,036 cr net block at Azad's own mature 1.13x turn supports ~Rs 1,100-1,200 cr revenue and Rs 175-215 cr PAT, at a returns-consistent 20-30x and discounted two years gives Rs 540-995/share. Leg 2, capital and returns: mature NOPAT of Rs 230-255 cr on invested capital of Rs 1,850-2,000 cr is 12-14% ROIC against a ~12% WACC, so growth is close to value-neutral and EV/IC belongs at 1.0-1.75x, giving Rs 236-445/share and stretching to only ~Rs 630 on materially better turns and working capital. The binding fact is that scale does not repair the return profile - even a Rs 2,000 cr-revenue FY31 case, built with the fixed assets and working capital it would require, still computes to ~13% ROIC - so I will not underwrite a franchise multiple however attractive the customer list; I defend Rs 350-700, centred ~Rs 500. At Rs 2,292 the market pays 111x trailing PAT, 9.7x book and 8.2x invested capital, a price that requires a ~56% sustainable ROE against the ~9% actually earned.

BALKRISIND.method_1: Normalised mid-cycle earnings multiple: mid-cycle EBITDA margin 24-25% (vs 4-yr actual range 17.5-24.1%) on revenue Rs 11,000-11,500 cr, less D&A ~Rs 875 cr, plus modest net other income, taxed at 25% gives normalised PAT Rs 1,320-1,650 cr = EPS Rs 68-85. Applied multiple 16-21x: above commodity tyre makers (MRF/Apollo/CEAT at 12-18x) because BKT has a genuine niche franchise with 51.7% gross margins and replacement-heavy off-highway demand, but well below Indian quality-ancillary compounder multiples of 25-35x because revenue CAGR is only ~3.5% and reinvestment absorbs most of the profit. Range: Rs 1,090-1,785 per share.
BALKRISIND.method_2: Balance-sheet / returns anchor (justified P/B via residual income): FY26 net worth Rs 10,955 cr on 19.33 cr shares = BVPS Rs 567. Sustainable ROE taken at 14-17% (4-yr actuals 14.0 / 16.6 / 15.9 / 11.3%, with upside allowed because a large slice of the current book is CWIP and under-utilised new capacity not yet earning), CoE 11.5-12.5% (Rf ~6.8%, ERP ~5.5%, beta ~0.9-1.0 for a cyclical exporter), long-run g 7-9%. Justified P/B = (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) cross-checked against a 10-15 year fading residual-income build gives 1.5-2.6x. Range: Rs 850-1,475 per share.
BALKRISIND.methods_are_independent: Leg 1 values the profit stream and says nothing about how much capital was consumed to produce it; Leg 2 is driven entirely by the size of the capital base and whether it earns a spread over cost of equity. For BKT specifically this is not a theoretical distinction: cumulative FY23-26 capex of Rs 7,347 cr against cumulative PAT of Rs 5,427 cr has grown the equity base faster than earnings, so the same profit now sits on a much larger book (ROE 11.3% in FY26 vs 16.6% in FY24). Leg 1 can be satisfied purely by a margin recovery with no view on the returns of the new assets; Leg 2 can only be satisfied if the Rs 3,003 cr of FY26 capex and the rest of the ramp actually earn above CoE. They did in fact diverge here - Leg 2 (850-1,475) sits materially below Leg 1 (1,090-1,785), which is the informative result: the P/B = P/E x ROE identity shows my 16-21x earnings multiple implicitly demands ~17-18% sustainable ROE, which is above what the last four years have delivered. I therefore leaned on Leg 1 for the centre while letting Leg 2 cap the top of the band. This is deliberately NOT a P/E-vs-EV/EBITDA pair, which would have been one method restated.
BALKRISIND.rationale: Leg 1 (normalised EPS Rs 68-85 at 16-21x) gives Rs 1,090-1,785; Leg 2 (justified P/B 1.5-2.6x on BVPS Rs 567 from sustainable ROE 14-17% vs CoE 11.5-12.5%) gives Rs 850-1,475; the overlap is Rs 1,090-1,475, which I widen to Rs 1,150-1,650 for genuine cyclical uncertainty since the ag-equipment downcycle may be near trough. Key figures: market cap Rs 47,813 cr and EV Rs 50,522 cr against FY26 revenue Rs 10,823 cr (+3.6%), EBITDA Rs 2,299 cr (21.2%, down from 24.1% in FY24), PAT Rs 1,243 cr (-25% YoY), capex Rs 3,003 cr (28% of revenue) producing FCF of -Rs 754 cr, book Rs 10,955 cr, ROE 11.3% and pre-tax ROCE 12.4% versus 17.5% a year earlier. BKT is a real franchise - FY26 gross margin actually rose to 51.7%, so the EBITDA compression is new-plant opex rather than lost pricing, and operating leverage should return as capacity fills - but at 22x EV/EBITDA and 38.5x trailing earnings the stock trades at a large premium to global off-highway peers (Michelin, Titan International, Nokian at 6-12x EV/EBITDA) on ~4% revenue growth and falling returns on capital. My triangulation is that Rs 2,473 already fully discounts a successful capex programme plus a full cyclical margin recovery to ~27% (revenue ~Rs 15,000 cr, PAT ~Rs 2,385 cr at 20x); discounting that outcome back 4-5 years at 12% yields ~Rs 1,459, squarely mid-band. Central judgement: fair value ~Rs 1,400, price is roughly 50% above the top of my band, so AVOID - the bull case is priced with no margin of safety for the cycle, the tariff/FX exposure or the unproven returns on the new asset base.

BANCOINDIA.method_1: Normalised earnings multiple. FY26 reported PAT 481.7 is flattered by non-operating income: PBT-EBIT+interest = 98.6 in FY26 vs 23.4/18.7/6.9 in FY25/24/23, and cash+ST investments averaged only ~220 so treasury cannot explain it (fixed assets also fell 518->477 despite capex 139 vs depreciation 134, suggesting a disposal gain or FX translation). Allowing ~35 of recurring other income gives normalised PAT ~434, EPS ~29.0 (on 14.97 cr shares; ~30.3 if the true count is 14.3 cr implied by Rs 28.61 cr capital at Rs 2 FV). Multiple 17-23x: justified P/E = (1 - g/ROE)/(CoE - g) spans 15-26x across CoE 12.5-13.5% and g 9-12% on ROE ~26-28%. A 29% ROCE niche cooling-systems franchise growing ~19% earns more than a commodity ancillary, but cyclical CV/tractor/off-highway exposure, EBITDA margin at a cyclical high (18.0% vs 15.5% two years ago) and a long-run ICE-cooling question cap it below a consumer-franchise rating. Range 493-690, central ~590.
BANCOINDIA.method_2: Observed free-cash-flow DCF. Base normalised FCF 220 = 3-yr average OCF 334 (FY24-26: 458.1, 164.3, 380.3) less normalised capex 130 (4-yr average 114.6, D&A 134.5). Grow 13% for five years, then let working-capital absorption ease as growth fades so terminal FCF reaches ~72% of PAT (vs ~50% today), WACC 11-12.5%, terminal g 5-6.5%, less net debt 406.8. Outputs: 341/sh at 12.5% WACC and 5% g, 427/sh at 12% and 6%, 581/sh at 11% and 6.5%. Cross-check on the observed record rather than the model: normalised FCF 220 against a 9,540 market cap is a 2.3% FCF yield, and EV 9,946 / EBITDA 702.7 = 14.2x for a peak-margin cyclical. Range 340-580, central ~450 (356-607 if the share count is 14.3 cr).
BANCOINDIA.methods_are_independent: They are not two views of the same number — they disagreed by ~28% at the centre (590 vs 450) and in one of the four years they moved in opposite directions outright: FY23 PAT was +235.6 while OCF was -41.5 and FCF -166.9. The wedge is structural, not noise. Cumulative FY23-26 PAT is 1,380.5 against cumulative FCF of 503.1 — 36% conversion — because growth is funded through the balance sheet: inventory 1,498 (140 days of revenue) and receivables 738 (69 days), so roughly half of each year's earnings is absorbed by incremental working capital before any capex. The earnings leg is structurally blind to that absorption (PAT is booked whether or not the cash arrives), while the cash leg is driven almost entirely by it. They also load on different risks: the P/E leg is sensitive to the other-income normalisation and to whether the 18% EBITDA margin holds; the FCF leg is sensitive to whether working-capital intensity ever releases. Either can be right with the other wrong — a margin-reversion scenario cuts the earnings leg while leaving the cash leg intact, and a working-capital release does the reverse. Note this is deliberately NOT a P/E-vs-EV/EBITDA pairing, which here would be near-tautological (EBITDA 702.7 maps to PAT 481.7 through fixed interest 22.6, D&A 134.5 and a 25.2% tax rate).
BANCOINDIA.rationale: Banco is a genuinely good niche auto ancillary — engine cooling and gaskets with a large European aftermarket arm — earning ~29% ROCE and ~32% ROE on average equity, growing revenue 19% CAGR to 3,896 with net debt of only 407 (0.58x EBITDA); it deserves a franchise-ish rating, not a commodity one. The normalised-earnings leg (17-23x on EPS ~29, after stripping ~65 of non-recurring other income from the 98.6 FY26 gap between PBT and EBIT-less-interest) gives 493-690; the observed-cash-flow leg (normalised FCF 220, WACC 11-12.5%, terminal g 5-6.5%) gives 340-580. The legs diverge because this business converts only ~36% of cumulative PAT into FCF, funding 19% growth through 140 days of inventory and 69 days of receivables — quality of earnings is the central question, and it argues for discounting the reported number rather than capitalising it. Their intersection is 490-600, which I widen modestly to 490-620 for the unresolved ~4.7% share-count ambiguity (28.61 capital at Rs 2 FV implies 14.3 cr shares, not the 14.97 supplied) and for margins sitting at a cyclical high. At 637.25 the stock trades at ~22x normalised earnings, 5.7x book, 14.2x EV/EBITDA and a 2.3% normalised FCF yield — sitting at or a hair above the top of my band, i.e. fully valued rather than clearly overvalued, so HOLD; a decisive REDUCE would be false precision at a 3% overshoot given the share-count noise.

BDL.method_1: Normalised through-cycle earnings multiple: steady-state revenue Rs 5,000 cr (from a ~Rs 22-25k cr order book, haircut for BDL's chronic under-execution) at 17-19% EBITDA margin, less D&A ~Rs 110 cr, plus ~Rs 350 cr of advance-float interest income, taxed at 26% gives normalised PAT of Rs 800-900 cr. Applied 32-42x - a deliberate discount to BEL/HAL (both ~26-27% ROE with clean delivery records) because BDL earns only 10-18% ROE under monopsony cost-plus pricing - giving Rs 25,600-37,800 cr equity value, i.e. Rs 700-1,030/share. No cash add-back, because the float's interest is already inside the earnings.
BDL.method_2: Steady-state free-cash-flow yield off the balance sheet: net operating capital is ~Rs 2,300 cr against Rs 2,442 cr of revenue (94% of sales), so growth self-consumes cash. Steady state FCF = PAT ~850 + D&A 110 - capex 250 - incremental working capital ~180 = ~Rs 530 cr base case; Rs 900 cr in the bull case where the Rs 4,626 cr inventory converts on a delivery step-up. Capitalised at a 3.0-4.0% demanded FCF yield (India 10y ~6.4%, so this already pays up heavily for the defence runway) gives Rs 12,500-30,000 cr, i.e. Rs 340-820/share.
BDL.methods_are_independent: They are independent because for BDL the P&L and the cash statement have physically decoupled, and the gap lives entirely on the balance sheet where no multiple can see it. FY26 PAT was Rs 420 cr while the three-year average FCF (excluding the FY23 advance-collection spike) was only ~Rs 197 cr - a 2x+ divergence created by the Rs 2,557 cr inventory build (2,068 to 4,626 over three years) and the MoD advance float, neither of which touches earnings. Leg 1 asserts what the business will accrue; Leg 2 asks how much of that ever converts to distributable cash given a working-capital cycle equal to 94% of revenue. They can only agree if the working capital stops absorbing, which is precisely the unresolved question, and in fact they disagreed by a factor of ~2 at the low end (Rs 700 vs Rs 340). This is not an earnings multiple restated: I deliberately avoided pairing P/E with EV/EBITDA, which for BDL would be near-tautological since interest expense is trivial (Rs 3.4 cr) and tax is a flat 26%.
BDL.rationale: Leg 1 (normalised PAT Rs 800-900 cr at 32-42x) gives Rs 700-1,030/share; Leg 2 (steady-state FCF Rs 530-900 cr at a 3.0-4.0% yield) gives Rs 340-820/share; the raw overlap is Rs 700-819, which I widen to Rs 640-880 because a 15%-wide band is false precision for a company whose revenue just fell 27% (3,329 to 2,442) and swings this violently year to year. Key figures: market cap Rs 45,926 cr on FY26 PAT of Rs 420 cr (109x trailing) and net worth of Rs 4,241 cr (10.8x book) against a four-year average ROE of only ~13.5%, versus a justified P/B of well under 3x on any sane cost of equity. The quality of earnings is the decisive point: FY26 PBT of Rs 568 cr came with EBIT of just Rs 147 cr, so roughly three-quarters of pre-tax profit was interest on the customer-advance float rather than missile manufacturing, while inventory grew another Rs 423 cr. An independent forward check - Rs 12,000 cr revenue by FY32 at 18% EBITDA, PAT ~Rs 1,800 cr at 35x, discounted six years at 12% - lands at Rs 873/share, right at my ceiling, meaning the top of my band already assumes the full air-defence upcycle executes cleanly. At Rs 1,253 the price sits ~42% above that ceiling and requires the everything-goes-right path (Rs 15,000 cr revenue at 20% margins on a 40x exit) from a company that has just missed badly, so AVOID.

BEML.method_1: Normalised-earnings multiple: margin-normalised PAT of Rs 218 cr (4-yr avg EBITDA margin 9.8% on FY26 revenue 4,351, less D&A 83, interest 45, tax 28% — matches the 4-yr PAT average of Rs 218 cr) up to a ramp-credited Rs 330 cr (revenue Rs 5,200 cr at 11.5% EBITDA margin). Applied 22-30x: 22x is fair for a 9-11% ROE, 4-6% growth industrial with poor cash conversion; 30x is a hard ceiling that already embeds a full defence-PSU / strategic-disinvestment premium (HAL trades ~30x on 25%+ ROE and net cash, which BEML does not have). Gives Rs 4,840-9,900 cr equity = Rs 580-1,190/share.
BEML.method_2: Balance-sheet / sustainable-ROE anchor (justified P/B): through-cycle ROE 8.4% (FY23 6.9%, FY24 11.1%, FY25 10.5%, FY26 4.9%), sustainable range 9-13% against CoE ~12.5-13% and g 5-6%. Strict Gordon (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) yields 0.5-1.2x book; lifted to 1.0-2.0x to credit the cyclically depressed current year, the ~3x-revenue order book and terminal defence-indigenisation optionality. On book rolled forward one year (Rs 2,934 cr + ~Rs 110 cr retained = Rs 3,044 cr, Rs 365/share) gives Rs 365-730/share.
BEML.methods_are_independent: Leg 1 capitalises normalised PROFIT and therefore rewards BEML for growing earnings; Leg 2 constrains value by the CAPITAL required to generate them and the return earned on it. They diverge exactly when a company buys earnings with balance sheet, which BEML does: net worth rose 21% and gross block 13% over FY23-26 while PAT fell from Rs 293 cr (FY25) to Rs 141 cr (FY26). They also respond oppositely to the live capex ramp — the earnings leg treats FY25-26's Rs 574 cr of capex as future profit, the book leg treats it as capital already charged to shareholders and demands a return on it. A cross-check confirms the divergence is real and not arithmetic: normalised owner cash flow (PAT 218 + D&A 83 - maintenance capex ~110 - incremental working capital ~130 at 5% growth) is only ~Rs 60-160 cr, because receivables run 251 days and net working capital is ~63% of revenue. A 20%-ROE business with 45-day receivables would see these two legs coincide; at 8-11% ROE with 251-day receivables they cannot. Notably I did NOT pair P/E with EV/EBITDA, which for BEML would be one method restated.
BEML.rationale: Normalised-earnings leg gives Rs 580-1,190/share (Rs 218-330 cr mid-cycle PAT at 22-30x); the sustainable-ROE book anchor gives Rs 365-730/share (1.0-2.0x a forward book of Rs 365/share on 9-13% ROE vs a ~13% CoE). Intersecting and widening for cyclical and capex-ramp uncertainty gives a defendable band of Rs 550-950. The core facts: 3-yr revenue CAGR of only 3.7% (3,899 to 4,351) despite a permanently live order-book narrative, EBITDA margin swinging 6.9-12.6%, through-cycle ROE 8.4%, negative FCF in FY25 (-94) and FY26 (-263), and net working capital at ~63% of revenue with receivables at 251 days. At Rs 1,750 the market cap of Rs 14,581 cr is 5.0x book, 103x trailing PAT, 50x even the FY25 peak PAT and ~35x normalised EBITDA, for a business whose post-tax return on capital sits below its cost of capital; the 2023 land demerger moved the surplus-asset optionality out of this entity, so nothing on the balance sheet rescues it. Even my most generous construction — revenue Rs 6,000 cr, 12-13% margin, PAT Rs 405-450 cr in FY29 at 25-30x, discounted back three years at 13% — reaches only ~Rs 840-1,125/share, so the price is not defensible on any reading of the financials.

BHEL.method_1: Normalised mid-cycle earnings power multiple: revenue normalised to ~Rs 45,000 cr (FY26 33,782 growing 19%, ~15% CAGR for 2 yrs on the order-book ramp) at a 6.5-9.0% normalised EBIT margin (FY26 actual 4.7%, trajectory 1.0/1.1/3.0/4.7) = EBIT 2,925-4,050; plus ~500 cr net treasury income (FY26 other income ~1,208 vs interest 665); tax 25% -> PAT 2,569-3,413, EPS 7.38-9.81 on 347.88 cr shares. Multiple 9-14x, derived from BHEL's OWN ~7-12% incremental ROIC vs ~13% CoE (Gordon-consistent P/E at 6.5% g is 5-9x; lifted to 9-14x for negligible PPE intensity, capex only 1.7% of sales, and order-book option value), NOT the 40-60x that 25%-ROE Indian capital-goods peers command. Range Rs 65-140.
BHEL.method_2: Justified P/B against sustainable ROE: BVPS = 26,146.6/347.88 = Rs 75.16. FY26 ROE 6.3% (PAT 1,600 on avg net worth 25,434); through-cycle sustainable ROE 9-13.5% including the loss-making downswings in BHEL's history. P/B = (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) with CoE 12.5-13% (Rf ~6.9%, ERP ~5.75%, beta >1 for a PSU cyclical) and g 5-6%: ROE 9% -> 0.53x -> Rs 40; ROE 11% -> 0.79x -> Rs 59; ROE 12.5% -> 1.00x -> Rs 75; ROE 13.5% -> 1.15x -> Rs 87. Range Rs 40-87.
BHEL.methods_are_independent: Yes, and they initially disagreed by 3x, which is the point. Leg 1 keys off the income statement — revenue trajectory times a normalised operating margin — and is structurally blind to how much capital is trapped generating that revenue. Leg 2 keys off the balance sheet — the size of the Rs 26,147 cr equity base and the sub-cost-of-equity return earned on it — and is blind to margin direction. They diverge whenever asset turns are abnormal, which is exactly BHEL's condition: total asset turn 0.44x (revenue 33,782 on assets 76,186), receivables at 239 days, and operating working capital swinging -155 -> 8,823 -> 9,703 -> 6,488 cr in three years. A margin-recovery story lifts Leg 1 without lifting Leg 2 when the recovery is bought with working capital; conversely FY26's 3,215 cr working-capital release plus 3,990 cr of customer advances lifted returns and cash flow without touching margins. Crucially these are NOT the forbidden P/E-vs-EV/EBITDA pairing: Leg 2 never touches PAT or EBITDA, only book value and return on it. My first pass gave Rs 150-260 vs Rs 40-87; forcing the earnings multiple to be derived from BHEL's measured ~7-12% incremental ROIC rather than borrowed from high-ROE peers collapsed Leg 1 to Rs 65-140 and produced a genuine overlap at Rs 65-87, which I widened to Rs 70-115 to weight the margin-step-change branch.
BHEL.rationale: Leg 1 (normalised earnings): Rs 45,000 cr normalised revenue at 6.5-9.0% EBIT plus ~500 cr treasury income gives normalised EPS of 7.38-9.81; at a fundamentals-consistent 9-14x (not the 40-60x of 25%-ROE peers, because BHEL's incremental ROIC is ~7-12% against a ~13% CoE) that is Rs 65-140. Leg 2 (justified P/B): BVPS Rs 75.16 with through-cycle ROE of 9-13.5% versus CoE 12.5-13% and g 5-6% gives 0.53-1.15x book, or Rs 40-87. The central judgement is that BHEL grows by consuming roughly 55-65 paise of working capital per rupee of incremental revenue while earning a 4.7% EBIT margin, so its growth is value-neutral at best and value-destructive at worst — the order-book runway is real but it is being converted at returns below the cost of the capital funding it, and FY26's headline 5,838 cr operating cash flow is advance-funded and working-capital-released, against a four-year average FCF of just 571 cr (0.40% yield on a 1,41,587 cr market cap). Even a genuinely excellent outcome — Rs 60,000 cr revenue by FY30 at a 10% EBIT margin, EPS ~14.4, exited at a generous 20x and discounted four years at 13% — values the equity near Rs 177, so the Rs 407 price requires PAT roughly 4.4x FY26 levels combined with a permanent franchise re-rating of a 6.3%-ROE PSU. I would defend Rs 70-115 (0.93-1.53x book, 7-12x normalised earnings) to a portfolio manager; at 88.5x trailing earnings and 72.7x EV/EBITDA the current price sits 3.5-5.8x above that band.

CANFINHOME.method_1: Justified P/B balance-sheet anchor: (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) with sustainable ROE 16-18.5%, g 8.5-9.5%, CoE ~13% -> 1.6-2.2x trailing book of Rs 448.98/sh = Rs 718-988
CANFINHOME.method_2: Normalised earnings multiple: 10.5-13.5x on tax-normalised EPS of Rs 78 (FY26 reported EPS 81.5 adjusted from a 16.7% tax rate to a 21% structural rate) = Rs 819-1,053
CANFINHOME.methods_are_independent: They are set from different evidence and can move in opposite directions on the same fact. Leg 1 values the EQUITY CAPITAL BASE by the spread between the return that capital earns and its cost; its swing factor is ROE fade — leverage is falling 8.52x -> 8.08x -> 7.42x because 84% retention outruns 8% book growth, and the FY26 spread windfall (NII +20.7% on 8.7% revenue growth) should partly reverse as loan yields reprice. Leg 2 values the EARNINGS STREAM by durability of ~10-13% growth against bank competition, benchmarked to HFC peers; its swing factor is the competitive question, not the capital question. The identity P/B = P/E x ROE only forces agreement if the earnings multiple is derived FROM the assumed ROE, which I did not do — and in fact the legs disagree, with Leg 2 roughly 10% higher at both ends. The divergence is structural: Can Fin's surplus capital (CRAR far above requirement) RAISES Leg 1's book base but LOWERS Leg 1's justified multiple via ROE dilution, while leaving Leg 2 almost untouched. I explicitly did NOT use a cash-flow or EV leg — for a lender OCF is dominated by disbursements (FY26 OCF is -2,910 cr purely because the book grew, vs +933 cr in FY25) and EV is meaningless when borrowings are raw material.
CANFINHOME.rationale: Can Fin Homes is a prime salaried-borrower HFC: FY26 PAT Rs 1,086 cr on net worth Rs 5,980 cr (avg ROE 19.7%, ROA 2.54%), 13.32 cr shares at Rs 820.6 = Rs 10,930 cr market cap, i.e. 1.83x trailing book and 10.1x reported EPS of Rs 81.5. The 20.5% three-year PAT CAGR flatters the franchise: total assets compounded only 10.3%, and the FY26 jump came from spread expansion (gross profit +20.7% on 8.7% revenue growth, with borrowing cost flat at ~Rs 2,570 cr) plus a 16.7% tax rate against 20-25% historically — normalising tax to 21% gives EPS ~Rs 78 and sustainable earnings growth nearer 10-13% than 20%. Leg 1, justified P/B of 1.6-2.2x on ROE 16-18.5% (faded for the 8.52x -> 7.42x leverage drift), g 8.5-9.5% and CoE ~13%, gives Rs 718-988. Leg 2, 10.5-13.5x normalised EPS — above LIC Housing's high-single-digit but well below the Aavas/Home First affordable niche, because Can Fin has best-in-class opex and ~30bp credit cost yet competes head-on with banks in prime home loans and has no pricing power — gives Rs 819-1,053. I defend Rs 790-1,000, centre ~Rs 895; at Rs 820.6 the stock sits in the cheap fifth of fair value, but ~9% upside to centre against a 13% cost of equity is not a margin of safety, so ACCUMULATE rather than BUY.

CARBORUNIV.method_1: Normalised-earnings multiple: through-cycle EBITDA margin 11.5-15% on FY26 revenue of 5,206 cr, less D&A 247 and interest 78, plus the persistent ~140 cr other income, taxed at 28%, giving normalised PAT of 300-430 cr (base ~360); applied at 24-30x for a mid-teens-through-cycle-ROE industrial consumables franchise => Rs 516-773/share.
CARBORUNIV.method_2: Owner cash-flow capitalisation: 4-year average operating cash flow of 426 cr less maintenance capex of ~215-250 cr (D&A 247, part of which is intangible amortisation on 219 cr intangibles / 297 cr goodwill) => owner FCF 150-270 cr; capitalised at a 4.5-5.5% required cash yield (r ~11.5%, g ~6.5%) plus 286 cr net cash => Rs 200-390/share.
CARBORUNIV.methods_are_independent: Leg 1 is an accrual-earnings measure; Leg 2 is a cash measure net of the capital the business actually consumes. They are not restatements of each other because the wedge between them is large and moving, not a fixed function: over FY23-26 cumulative PAT was 1,384 cr against cumulative FCF of 578 cr (42% conversion), because gross block rose 49% (1,910 -> 2,848) and inventory plus receivables absorbed ~475 cr while revenue grew only 12%. The earnings leg credits the profit the enlarged asset base should eventually produce; the cash leg charges for the cash the ramp has already burned. They in fact diverge by roughly 2x here (516-773 vs 200-390), which is the diagnostic the two-leg design exists to surface. I deliberately avoided pairing P/E with EV/EBITDA off the same year, which would have been one method twice. A justified-P/B cross-check (ROE 13%, CoE 12%, g 6% => ~1.2x book, Rs ~280; ROE 16%, CoE 11.5%, g 7% => ~2.0x, Rs ~479) corroborates the cash leg's direction rather than the earnings leg's.
CARBORUNIV.rationale: CUMI is a three-part industrial materials business (branded abrasives, engineered ceramics, and commodity electrominerals including the Russian silicon-carbide operation) in a genuine two-year earnings collapse: EBITDA margin fell 16.3% (FY24) -> 12.5% (FY25) -> 8.6% (FY26) while revenue only crept 4,702 -> 5,206 cr, so PAT dropped 476 -> 168 and ROE went ~16% -> 4.5% on 3,900 cr of net worth. Leg 1 (normalised earnings) puts through-cycle PAT at 300-430 cr and at 24-30x yields Rs 516-773/share; Leg 2 (owner cash flow of 150-270 cr at a 4.5-5.5% cash yield, plus 286 cr net cash) yields Rs 200-390/share. The ~2x disagreement is the real finding: cumulative FY23-26 PAT of 1,384 cr produced only 578 cr of FCF, and a 49% gross-block expansion to 2,848 cr has so far generated no incremental EBITDA at all, so I will not pay for the capex ramp on faith. Blending 55/45 toward earnings gives equity value of ~6,500-10,100 cr, i.e. Rs 380-600/share; the band is wide because the legs genuinely conflict, and it straddles the share-count ambiguity (Re 1 equity capital of 19.05 cr implies ~19.05 cr shares versus the 16.29 cr supplied, a ~15% per-share difference). At Rs 1,064 the market pays roughly 3.3-3.9x sales, 4.4-5.2x book, and over 35x even a full recovery to FY24 peak earnings of 476 cr - a level no reconstruction of this four-year record supports, hence AVOID rather than merely REDUCE.

CARRARO.method_1: NORMALISED (MID-CYCLE) EARNINGS MULTIPLE. FY26 PBT 172.78 vs EBIT 163.74 less interest 19.48 implies Rs 28.5cr of other income against a Rs 12-14cr three-year run-rate; stripping the excess and taxing at 24.5% gives clean FY26 PAT ~Rs 119.5cr, EPS Rs 21.0 (reported EPS Rs 22.95). FY26 revenue of 2,255 is 20% above the four-year average and 25% above FY25, so I treat it as at/near a cyclical high for tractors and construction equipment, but credit the structural EBITDA-margin climb (5.9% -> 7.6% -> 9.6% -> 9.3%) as durable rather than cyclical. Normalised EPS band Rs 19.5-21.5 (centre 20.5). Multiple 17-24x: justified by 25.5% ROE, 19.7% post-tax ROIC and 0.30x net-debt/EBITDA, but capped well below franchise ancillary multiples (30x+) because a 9.3% EBITDA margin is thin machining/assembly economics, end-markets are cyclical, and the float is small with the Italian parent dominant and material related-party export supply. Range: Rs 350-500, centre ~Rs 410.
CARRARO.method_2: OWNER CASH FLOW / SUSTAINABLE FCF YIELD. Normalised OCF = clean PAT 119.5 + D&A 45.7 less steady-state working-capital investment (core WC has run 12-14% of sales; at 6-12% revenue growth that absorbs Rs 16-33cr) = Rs 133-149cr. Normalised capex Rs 60-75cr, NOT the FY26 figure: FY26 capex of Rs 32.2cr was only 0.71x depreciation on a net block that actually shrank (353.6 -> 351.6) while revenue grew 25%, so FY26's Rs 102cr reported FCF is borrowed from a capex holiday at what must now be high utilisation; FY23-24 capex ran 1.7-2.0x depreciation and capex has averaged ~3.5% of sales. Sustainable FCF ~Rs 65-90cr, centre ~Rs 80cr. Capitalised at a 3.7-4.8% required yield (21-27x) for a ~10%-growth, 20%-ROIC but cyclical and illiquid small-cap industrial. Range: Rs 280-420, centre ~Rs 340. (Cross-check only, not a third leg: justified P/B = (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) at sustainable ROE 20-22%, g 8-10%, CoE 12.5% gives 2.7-4.8x on book of Rs 99.2/sh = Rs 265-476 — straddles both legs and does not rescue the current price.)
CARRARO.methods_are_independent: They can and do diverge because this company converts accounting profit into cash at roughly half the rate the P&L implies, so the two legs are driven by different variables rather than the same one restated. Over FY23-26 cumulative PAT was Rs 328cr but cumulative FCF was only Rs 162cr — 49% conversion — because core working capital (receivables + inventory - payables) rose from Rs 130cr to Rs 272cr, i.e. from 7.7% to 12.1% of sales, absorbing ~Rs 142cr, while capex of Rs 233cr ran 1.36x the Rs 172cr of depreciation. The earnings leg rewards the reported PAT ramp (41% three-year CAGR) and is blind to that absorption; the cash leg charges it and additionally refuses to extrapolate FY26's sub-maintenance capex, which the earnings leg never sees. That is why they land Rs 410 vs Rs 340 at their centres — a ~20% gap that is the actual investment question, not a rounding artefact. I deliberately did NOT pair P/E with EV/EBITDA: I computed both and they reconcile (11x mid-cycle EBITDA implies ~19x post-tax EBIT, i.e. essentially the same answer as 20x earnings), confirming they are one leg restated and worthless as corroboration here.
CARRARO.rationale: Leg 1 (normalised earnings, EPS Rs 19.5-21.5 at 17-24x) gives Rs 350-500; Leg 2 (sustainable FCF Rs 65-90cr at a 3.7-4.8% required yield) gives Rs 280-420; the defensible intersection is Rs 350-440, midpoint ~Rs 395, and a justified-P/B cross-check of Rs 265-476 sits astride it without lifting it. Key figures: market cap Rs 3,052cr on 5.69cr shares, EV Rs 3,114cr, FY26 revenue 2,255 (+24.8%), EBITDA 209.4 (9.3%), reported PAT 130.6, clean PAT ~119.5, net worth 564.6, net debt 62.4 (0.30x EBITDA), ROE 25.5%, post-tax ROIC 19.7%, four-year FCF/PAT 49%. This is a genuinely improving Tier-1 driveline supplier to tractor and construction-equipment OEMs — margins have nearly doubled in three years, the balance sheet is clean and deleveraging, and returns on capital are good — but it is a 9%-EBITDA-margin cyclical with a working-capital habit, a coming capex cycle, and an Italian parent on both the register and the customer list, so it earns a solid mid-teens-to-low-twenties multiple, not a franchise one. At Rs 536 the market is paying 23.4x what looks like peak EPS, 14.9x peak EBITDA, 5.4x book and a 2.6% normalised FCF yield, which requires FY26 margins to hold AND cash conversion to repair AND the tractor/CE cycle not to turn — three things at once. My band sits 18% below the current price at its top and I would trim into this strength rather than underwrite all three.

CGCL.method_1: Normalised earnings multiple. FY26 reported PAT of Rs 949 cr is normalised down to ~Rs 800 cr (EPS ~Rs 8.5 on 93.79 cr shares) after stripping a suspected ~Rs 375 cr pre-tax non-operating/exceptional gain: the FY26 record shows PBT 1,257.41 vs EBIT 882.54, a 375 cr gap, whereas FY23/24/25 all satisfy PBT = EBIT - interest_expense exactly; corroborated independently by ROA jumping 2.66% -> 3.55% and PAT/net-total-income jumping 25.7% -> 38.2% in a single year. Applied multiple 15-20x: the 22-25x end (Home First, Cholamandalam) is unwarranted given mid-tier asset quality, an unseasoned rapid gold-loan build and a ROE that only just crossed 16%; the 12-14x end (Shriram, LIC HF) is too harsh given 25-30% earnings growth and a genuinely capital-light fee stream from car-loan distribution. Range: Rs 128-171/share (central ~17x = Rs 145).
CGCL.method_2: Balance-sheet anchor via justified P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) on stated book. BVPS = Rs 76.80 (net worth Rs 7,203.48 cr / 93.79 cr shares). Sustainable ROE 15-17% (peak achieved 16.5% on average equity, but the post-QIP book is fat and under-levered at borrowings/net worth of only 3.35x, so near-term ROE on year-end book is ~12-13% and rises as leverage normalises); CoE 13.0-13.5% (Rf ~6.75%, ERP ~5.5%, beta ~1.2 plus a mid-cap liquidity premium); terminal g 9.0-9.5% nominal. Justified P/B = 1.33x to 2.14x -> Rs 102-164/share, central ~Rs 130. Cross-checked with a 10-year two-stage residual-income model (BV0 7,203 cr, average ROE 15.3%, book growth ~14.8% at 3% payout, CoE 13.5%, terminal P/B 1.11x): V0 = 7,203 + 1,204 PV(RI) + 889 PV(terminal excess) = Rs 9,296 cr, or ~Rs 99/share -- low because a ~2pp ROE-CoE spread makes even 15% book compounding close to value-neutral.
CGCL.methods_are_independent: Yes, and they demonstrably diverged. Leg 1 is a market-comparable multiple on a FLOW whose central uncertainty is earnings quality -- how much of FY26's Rs 949 cr PAT repeats. Leg 2 is a theory-derived anchor on a STOCK (stated net worth) and is completely insensitive to whether FY26's reported PAT was clean; its uncertainty lives entirely in the CoE-minus-g spread and sustainable ROE. Crucially the P/B = P/E x ROE identity does NOT collapse them here, because the two legs run on different ROEs: Leg 1's normalised EPS of Rs 8.5 implies only ~11% ROE on the year-end book, while Leg 2 assumes 15-17% sustainable once the freshly raised QIP capital is levered up (net worth rose 67% YoY to 7,203 cr on only ~14% more shares, so the flow and the stock are temporarily out of step). That gap is real, not arithmetic: Leg 2's central (Rs 130) landed ~10% below Leg 1's (Rs 145), and had I taken FY26 PAT at face value Leg 1 would have printed Rs 152-202 while Leg 2 was unchanged -- a 2x spread at the low end is reachable within each leg's own assumption set. I deliberately did NOT pair P/E with EV/EBITDA (mechanically linked, and meaningless for a lender anyway), and I rejected a cash-flow leg outright: operating CF of -8,728 cr is loan-book disbursement, not economic burn, so FCF carries no valuation signal for an NBFC.
CGCL.rationale: Capri Global is a fast-scaling secured NBFC -- MSME/LAP, gold loans, affordable housing plus a capital-light car-loan distribution book -- with total assets compounding 11,801 -> 15,150 -> 20,831 -> 32,676 cr, net total income (revenue less finance cost) 921 -> 2,483 cr, and ROE on average equity improving 6% -> 7.5% -> 11.8% -> 16.5% as the FY23-24 branch build-out turns into operating leverage. I do not take FY26's reported PAT of Rs 949 cr at face value: PBT (1,257.41) exceeds EBIT (882.54) by 375 cr where every prior year had PBT = EBIT - interest, and two independent checks agree it is flattered (ROA 2.66% -> 3.55%, PAT/NTI 25.7% -> 38.2%), so I normalise to ~Rs 800 cr, EPS ~Rs 8.5. Leg 1 (earnings multiple, 15-20x on normalised EPS) gives Rs 128-171; Leg 2 (justified P/B on BVPS Rs 76.80 with sustainable ROE 15-17%, CoE 13.0-13.5%, g 9.0-9.5%, i.e. 1.33-2.14x) gives Rs 102-164, with a two-stage residual-income cross-check at ~Rs 99 because a ~2pp ROE-CoE spread makes rapid book growth nearly value-neutral. Intersecting the two, I would defend Rs 130-172 to a PM, widened slightly for the earnings-quality uncertainty and the share-count ambiguity (93.79 cr shares vs Rs 96.22 cr of equity capital at Re 1 face value, a ~2.6% dilution overhang). At Rs 232.38 the market pays 3.03x book, which at a 4.5pp CoE-minus-g spread requires ~21% sustainable ROE -- a level Capri has never earned, its peak being 16.5% on average equity in a year I believe contains a one-off -- so the price sits ~35% above my top and the call is REDUCE, not AVOID, since the underlying franchise is sound and genuinely compounding.

CHOICEIN.method_1: Normalised earnings multiple: 18-26x on ~Rs 235 cr normalised-forward consolidated PAT (between FY26 trailing Rs 217.7 cr and FY27E ~Rs 260 cr, haircut for earnings quality). Multiple anchored on Indian financial-services comps - Angel One/Motilal Oswal ~12-18x, Nuvama ~18-22x, 360 One ~30x, Anand Rathi ~50x. Choice is a sub-scale full-service broker plus government-advisory plus small NBFC with no durable moat and a conglomerate structure, so mid-range, not franchise. Yields Rs 3,780-6,110 cr equity value = Rs 218-315/sh. Cross-checked against a 5-yr bull DCF (25% PAT CAGR, 20x exit, 14% discount) = Rs 357/sh.
CHOICEIN.method_2: Balance-sheet anchor: justified P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) plus an explicit 10-year residual-income build. Sustainable ROE 16-18% (FY26 realised 16.1% on average equity, 13.0% on ending equity, trending down from 23.6% in FY24), CoE 12.0-14.5% (Rf ~7%, ERP ~6%, beta 1.2-1.4 plus small-cap/governance premium), g 7-8%. Gives justified P/B of 1.3-2.5x; the RI build at CoE 14.5% / ROE 17% fading to 15% returns Rs 2,154 cr = 1.29x book. Applied to FY26 net worth of Rs 1,671.5 cr: Rs 1,890-4,180 cr = Rs 111-216/sh.
CHOICEIN.methods_are_independent: They share the identity P/E = P/B / ROE but are anchored on different inputs and did in fact diverge, overlapping only at the extreme edge (~Rs 215-220). Leg 1 imports a peer earnings multiple that prices the P&L growth rate and is silent on the capital consumed to produce it. Leg 2 prices only the spread of realised ROE over cost of equity and is indifferent to headline growth. For Choice these pull hard in opposite directions because the growth is capital-funded: net worth tripled from Rs 477 cr to Rs 1,672 cr in three years via repeated equity issuance (share capital 199.66 to 222.78) while ROE FELL from 23.6% to 16.1%, and cumulative four-year operating cash flow is NEGATIVE (-Rs 156 cr) against Rs 571 cr of cumulative reported PAT. Leg 1 rewards the 34% PAT growth; leg 2 punishes the falling return on the equity that bought it. Leg 1 at 18-26x on 17% ROE implies 3.1-4.4x book versus leg 2's 1.3-2.5x - a genuine 2x gap, not arithmetic. I deliberately avoided an FCF-yield leg (FCF was -164, -451, +46 cr across FY24-26 because loan-book and margin-funding growth run through operating cash flow, so it would be noise not a second opinion) and avoided EV/EBITDA (interest expense of Rs 89 cr, 5x FY23, is raw material for the lending arm, and net debt is contaminated by client float - Rs 880 cr cash against Rs 753 cr of other current liabilities).
CHOICEIN.rationale: Choice International is a diversified small-cap financial group - full-service broking, a government/infrastructure advisory arm driving the margin expansion (EBITDA margin 27.2% to 35.7%), and a capital-hungry NBFC/margin-funding book - growing fast (revenue Rs 385 to Rs 1,119 cr, PAT Rs 60 to Rs 218 cr over FY23-26) but with visibly deteriorating capital efficiency and cash conversion. Leg 1 (18-26x on ~Rs 235 cr normalised-forward PAT) gives Rs 218-315/sh; leg 2 (justified P/B 1.3-2.5x, RI-anchored, on Rs 1,671.5 cr net worth at 16-18% sustainable ROE against a 12-14.5% CoE) gives Rs 111-216/sh; I settle at Rs 175-300, weighting the balance-sheet leg more heavily because ROE is falling, equity is being issued serially, receivables have run to 142 days (Rs 437 cr = 39% of revenue) and cumulative four-year OCF is negative. That band is Rs 3,390-5,820 cr, or roughly 16-27x trailing PAT and 2.0-3.5x book - already generous for a 16%-ROE, low-moat financial conglomerate. The market is paying Rs 15,949 cr: 73x trailing earnings, 9.5x book and 14.3x sales, versus ~3-4x sales for Angel One and ~8x for 360 One, and even a bull case of 25% PAT CAGR for five years at a 20x exit discounted at 14% only reaches Rs 357/sh - justifying Rs 823 requires a 46x exit multiple. One caveat that only strengthens the call: FY26 share capital of Rs 222.78 cr at Rs 10 face value implies ~22.3 cr shares versus the 19.38 cr supplied, so true per-share value is likely ~13% below my band.

CIEINDIA.method_1: Normalised earnings multiple. Core operating PAT stripped of other income: EBIT normalised to ~Rs 1,080 cr (FY23 1,127 / FY24 1,095 / FY25 1,039 — FY25 is a soft print on a weak Europe) less interest Rs 45 cr, taxed at the actual 23.9% rate = Rs 788 cr. Multiple range 13-17x, deliberately BELOW the Indian auto-ancillary cohort (which trades 22-30x on 12-15% growth) because CIEINDIA's revenue CAGR is 2.4% over FY22-25, EBIT has DECLINED 8% since FY23, ~40%+ of the book is tied to a structurally shrinking European auto market, and ROIC including the Rs 3,038 cr acquisition goodwill is only 12.7%. Ops value Rs 10,240-13,390 cr, plus reported net cash Rs 1,211 cr (cash 1,635 less borrowings 426) = equity Rs 11,450-14,600 cr, or Rs 302-385/share, central ~Rs 343 at 15x.
CIEINDIA.method_2: Owner-earnings cash-flow value. Normalised FCF from OCF less maintenance capex: 4-yr OCF averages Rs 1,160 cr; capex has converged on depreciation (capex/dep 1.69 -> 1.65 -> 1.17 -> 1.05), so maintenance capex ~Rs 400 cr against D&A of Rs 358 cr. Realised FCF was 617 / 853 / 494 / 881 over FY22-25, 4-yr mean Rs 711 cr; normalised band Rs 620-800 cr. Discounted 5 years then terminal: bear Rs 620 cr at 2% then 2.5% terminal, CoE 13% = Rs 188/sh; base Rs 720 cr at 5% then 4%, CoE 12% = Rs 289/sh; bull Rs 800 cr at 7% then 5%, CoE 11.5% = Rs 403/sh. All include net cash of Rs 1,211 cr. Defensible interquartile Rs 250-345, central ~Rs 289.
CIEINDIA.methods_are_independent: Yes, and they demonstrably disagreed here (central 343 vs 289, ~19% apart). The earnings-multiple leg capitalises an accrual profit figure and is structurally blind to capital intensity, working-capital swings and the QUALITY of reinvestment; the cash-flow leg is an absolute discounting exercise whose answer is driven by capex-versus-depreciation, working capital, and the CoE/growth spread — inputs the multiple never sees. The divergence is not hypothetical in this name: identical PAT of Rs 820 cr (FY24) and Rs 823 cr (FY25) mapped to FCF of Rs 494 cr and Rs 881 cr respectively, a 60% versus 107% conversion, so the same earnings number produces two very different cash answers. The DCF also prices in a fact the multiple hides: FY23-25 retained equity of Rs 1,471 cr generated only Rs 25 cr of incremental PAT (1.7% incremental ROE) because the retention went into an idle cash pile, which caps sustainable growth in the discounting leg while leaving the P/E untouched. Note this is deliberately NOT a P/E-versus-EV/EBITDA pairing, which would be one method restated.
CIEINDIA.rationale: CIE India is a well-run but no-growth Tier-1 auto component supplier: revenue Rs 9,406 cr growing 2.4% CAGR since FY22, EBITDA margin stable at 14.9-15.9%, PAT stuck at Rs 798/820/823 cr for three straight years, and ROE decaying 13.9% -> 11.0% purely because equity compounds into cash while profit does not. It carries Rs 1,211 cr net cash and Rs 3,038 cr of acquisition goodwill; ROIC is 12.7% on total capital (24.6% ex-goodwill), i.e. the operating business is genuinely good but the price paid for it was full, and roughly 40%+ exposure to a shrinking European auto market is a real structural drag. The earnings leg at 13-17x normalised core operating PAT of Rs 788 cr plus net cash gives Rs 302-385; the owner-earnings DCF on normalised FCF of Rs 620-800 cr at 11.5-13% CoE gives Rs 250-345 on its defensible interquartile (Rs 188-403 full range); a justified-P/B cross-check on 11% stated ROE / 18.7% ROTE lands lower still at Rs 172-213, which I weight only as a caution flag given goodwill and idle-cash distortion. Intersecting the two primary legs I would defend Rs 290-370, central ~Rs 325, implying 15x earnings, 8x EV/EBITDA and a 5.7% normalised FCF yield — fair for a flat-earnings cyclical with a cash cushion. At Rs 408.6 (18.8x earnings, 10.2x EV/EBITDA, 2.08x book, 4.6% normalised FCF yield) the stock sits ~10% above my band top and ~26% above centre, so the price is paying a growth multiple for a business that has not grown its profit in three years: REDUCE.

COCHINSHIP.method_1: Normalised mid-cycle earnings multiple: 18-26x on Rs 750-900 cr normalised PAT (FY24-26 avg 776 cr, FY26 717 cr), giving Rs 513-889/sh. Multiple set below a franchise cap-goods rating because of PSU margin caps, 13.7-24.2% EBITDA-margin volatility across four years, and contract lumpiness.
COCHINSHIP.method_2: Balance-sheet anchor: justified P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) on BVPS Rs 223.2, with sustainable ROE 14-18%, CoE 12.0-13.5%, long-run g 7.5-8% => 1.08x-2.50x => Rs 241-558/sh; cross-checked with a two-stage residual-income model (B0 5,873 cr, PAT 850->1,800 cr by FY31, ROE ramping to 20% on the new dry dock/ISRF, CoE 12.5%, terminal RI growth 6%) which tops out at Rs 508/sh.
COCHINSHIP.methods_are_independent: Yes. I deliberately did NOT pair P/E with EV/EBITDA — off the same year those are one leg restated, since PAT is a fixed function of EBITDA once D&A, interest and tax are set. The earnings-multiple leg is agnostic to how much capital was consumed to produce the profit: it prices the income statement and embeds a view on growth durability. The P/B-residual-income leg does the opposite — it explicitly penalises an earnings stream generated on a heavy, fast-compounding equity base at a return only 1-3pp above cost of equity, and is driven by ROE, CoE and retention rather than by any multiple. They can and did diverge sharply here (Rs 513-889 vs Rs 240-558, roughly 2x apart, overlapping only at the edges) precisely because CSL's equity base is growing faster than its profit (ROE 16.6% -> 15.6% -> 12.5%), which the P/E leg cannot see and the P/B leg is built to catch. I considered an FCF-yield leg instead but rejected it as unusable: operating cash flow was negative in all three of FY24 (-172 cr), FY25 (-297 cr) and FY26 (-1,234 cr), so there is no positive cash stream to capitalise — that fact instead informs the haircut applied to the earnings multiple in Leg 1.
COCHINSHIP.rationale: Normalised-earnings leg: mid-cycle PAT of Rs 750-900 cr (FY24-26 average 776 cr; FY26 717 cr after EBITDA margin collapsed from 24.2% to 16.2% on just 5% revenue growth) at 18-26x gives Rs 513-889/sh. Balance-sheet leg: BVPS Rs 223.2 (net worth 5,872.76 cr / 26.31 cr shares) with sustainable ROE 14-18% against a 12-13.5% cost of equity and 7.5-8% long-run growth implies justified P/B of 1.08-2.50x, i.e. Rs 241-558, and even a bullish two-stage residual-income run with ROE ramping to 20% on the newly commissioned dry dock and ISRF tops out near Rs 508. The two legs overlap only at Rs 513-555, so I widen modestly to Rs 480-690 to respect parameter uncertainty and genuine Indian-shipbuilding-cycle optionality (customer advances of 5,906 cr exceed a full year of revenue, confirming a deep order book). The decisive judgement is cash quality: operating cash flow was -172, -297 and -1,234 cr in FY24/25/26 against 2,327 cr of cumulative reported PAT, with inventory up 373->2,288 cr and other current assets 178->5,278 cr, so profits are ship WIP and unbilled contract assets rather than cash, and the equity base is compounding faster than earnings. At Rs 1,423 the stock is 52x trailing PAT and 6.4x book for a 12.5%-ROE, negative-FCF PSU yard — that price only works if earnings roughly triple by FY31 and still exit at 25x, which is the bull case being paid for as the base case.

CREDITACC.method_1: NORMALISED-EARNINGS MULTIPLE (P&L lens). FY26 pre-provision operating profit = total income 6,010 - interest 1,896 - opex (sga 1,234 + dep 63) = Rs 2,816 cr. FY26 credit cost is still Rs 1,783 cr (~6.0% of average assets, ~6.4% of a ~Rs 28,000 cr book) — crisis-level, versus Rs 461 cr (1.8%) in FY24. Normalising credit cost to 3.0-3.5% of book (a through-cycle rate for an NBFC-MFI that includes periodic blow-ups, not the 1.5-2% booked in benign years) gives mid-cycle PAT of Rs 1,380-1,480 cr, i.e. EPS ~Rs 86-92 on 16.05 cr shares; I use Rs 90. Multiple 11-16x: the theoretical lender P/E = payout/(CoE-g) = (1 - g/ROE)/(CoE-g) gives 11-12x at ROE 18%, g 10%, CoE 14%, while CREDITACC has historically traded 15-19x trailing in good years as the scale leader with the sector's lowest opex ratio. Range: Rs 990 - Rs 1,440.
CREDITACC.method_2: STRESSED ADJUSTED-BOOK ANCHOR (balance-sheet lens). Reported net worth FY26 Rs 7,842 cr = BVPS Rs 489. Strip goodwill Rs 376 cr (Madura acquisition) and intangibles Rs 81 cr: tangible book Rs 7,386 cr = TBVPS Rs 460. The credit cycle is demonstrably unfinished — FY26 credit cost is still ~6% of assets, only marginally below FY25's 6.8% — so I charge one further year of above-normal loss (~4% vs 2.5-3% normal, ~Rs 420 cr pre-tax / ~Rs 315 cr post-tax), giving stressed tangible book of ~Rs 7,070 cr = Rs 440/share. Applied P/TB of 1.6-2.6x, anchored on what an unsecured, uncollateralised, politically-exposed JLG franchise is worth to an acquirer, with the top of the range reserved for the scale leader. Range: Rs 700 - Rs 1,150. Cross-checked with a 10-year residual-income build off Rs 7,842 cr book: bear (CoE 14.5%, ROE path 13%->17% fading to 14.75%) Rs 562; base (CoE 14%, peak 18.5%) Rs 779; bull (CoE 13.5%, peak 19.5%, 2% terminal spread) Rs 972.
CREDITACC.methods_are_independent: Leg 1 asks "what does this franchise earn once the credit cycle turns" — its swing variable is the normalised credit-cost rate applied to a P&L that is currently 6%-of-book impaired. Leg 2 asks "how much real capital actually stands behind the equity, and what does a buyer pay for that capital base" — its swing variables are goodwill/intangible strip, residual under-provisioning in the loan book, and franchise transaction evidence. They diverge sharply in both directions: if the book is under-provided or the Karnataka/MFI stress runs another two years, Leg 2 collapses toward 1.4-1.6x tangible book (~Rs 620-700) while Leg 1 still prints Rs 1,200+ because it assumes credit costs mean-revert on schedule; conversely, a fortress balance sheet with permanently lower post-guardrail growth would hold Leg 2 up while Leg 1's multiple compresses toward the 11x theoretical floor. They in fact DID disagree here — centres of Rs 1,215 vs Rs 925, a 31% gap, and the RI cross-check (Rs 562-972) sits entirely below Leg 1's range. Critically, I did NOT derive Leg 2's P/TB from Leg 1's ROE via the Gordon identity (justified P/B = P/E x ROE), which would have made them one equation restated; Leg 2's multiple is grounded in stressed asset value and MFI franchise pricing, and its book input (FY26 balance sheet, already struck) is a realised number while Leg 1's earnings input is a forecast. Note the residual honest linkage: P/B and P/E are connected through ROE, but here trailing ROE is 10.5% while normalised ROE is ~18-19%, so the two legs are keyed off genuinely different states of the business rather than the same year's arithmetic.
CREDITACC.rationale: CreditAccess Grameen is India's largest NBFC-MFI — best-in-class opex, 4.0-4.3x leverage, and a demonstrated 24.8% ROE in FY24 — but it is two years into a severe microfinance credit event: ROE fell to 7.9% (FY25) and has only recovered to 10.5% (FY26), with credit costs still running ~6% of assets versus 1.8% in FY24, and PPOP growth (2,400 -> 2,641 -> 2,816) doing all the work while the loss line eats it. Leg 1 (normalised EPS ~Rs 90 at 11-16x) gives Rs 990-1,440; Leg 2 (stressed tangible book Rs 440 at 1.6-2.6x P/TB) gives Rs 700-1,150; the mechanical intersection of Rs 990-1,150 is too narrow to be honest given the legs' centres are 31% apart, and a 10-year residual-income cross-check (Rs 562-972 across CoE 13.5-14.5%) sits below both, so I widen to Rs 880-1,260 — 1.8-2.6x reported book, 2.0-2.9x stressed tangible book, 9.8-14.0x mid-cycle earnings. At Rs 1,592.8 the market is paying 3.26x book, 3.6x stressed tangible book and 32.9x trailing FY26 earnings for a lender whose current ROE is 10.5%, which prices a full snap-back to 19%+ ROE as already delivered; even my bull residual-income path with a 13.5% CoE cannot reach Rs 1,000. The price is ~26% above my upper bound: REDUCE rather than AVOID, because the underlying franchise is genuinely the sector's best and a faster-than-modelled normalisation would close much of the gap.

ELGIEQUIP.method_1: Normalised core-earnings multiple: strip the ~Rs117cr of non-operating other income thrown off by the Rs950cr cash pile, giving core operating PAT of ~Rs343cr on FY26 (Rs365cr if EBITDA margin normalises back to 15%). Applied 24-32x — a genuine engineering franchise (air compressors, aftermarket annuity, 21% ROE, 26% pre-tax ROCE, net cash) but NOT a 40x compounder given 5.1% PAT CAGR over FY23-26 and 350bp of EBITDA margin erosion (17.8%->14.3%). Adds back Rs575cr of cash and non-current investments separately. Range Rs279-388/sh.
ELGIEQUIP.method_2: Cash-flow leg: two-stage DCF on sustainable free cash flow. Sustainable FCF anchored at Rs280-320cr (reported FY24-26 FCF Rs236/296/299cr; avg OCF Rs376cr less maintenance capex ~= D&A Rs86-90cr gives Rs286cr). Stage 1 growth 10-12% for 5 years, terminal 5.5-6.0%, CoE 10.5-11.5% (Indian RFR ~6.75%, ERP ~5%, beta ~0.9 for a net-cash industrial). Yields EV Rs5,900-9,700cr; plus Rs575cr cash/investments gives Rs220-330/sh, centre ~Rs275.
ELGIEQUIP.methods_are_independent: Yes, and they demonstrably disagree (centres Rs333 vs Rs275, a 21% gap). The earnings leg is driven by the multiple applied to accounting profit; the cash-flow leg is driven by three inputs that never touch the P/E: (1) working-capital intensity — NWC of Rs983cr is 24.9% of revenue, so 10-12% revenue growth absorbs ~Rs100cr/yr of cash that PAT never sees; (2) capex running at 1.8x D&A (Rs154.4cr vs Rs85.8cr) during a facility ramp, so reported FCF is only ~70% of PAT; (3) the discount rate and fade profile. Change the WC assumption or CoE by 100bp and the cash-flow leg moves 25-30% while the earnings leg does not move at all. I deliberately did NOT pair P/E with EV/EBITDA — on FY26 figures those are mechanically the same statement (PAT is EBITDA less fixed D&A/interest/tax). An independent third check, justified P/B = (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) on 20% sustainable ROE, gives Rs204-311/sh and corroborates the lower half of the band.
ELGIEQUIP.rationale: ELGI is a real business — India's #2 air compressor maker with global reach, net cash of Rs417cr, 21% ROE and 26% pre-tax ROCE — but the trajectory does not support a franchise multiple: revenue compounded 9.1% over FY23-26 while PAT compounded only 5.1% (Rs371cr -> Rs430cr) because EBITDA margin fell from 17.8% to 14.3%, and roughly Rs117cr of FY26's PBT is other income on the cash hoard rather than operations. The normalised-earnings leg (core PAT Rs343-365cr at 24-32x, plus Rs575cr cash/investments) gives Rs279-388/sh; the cash-flow leg (sustainable FCF Rs280-320cr, 10-12% for 5 years fading to 5.5-6%, CoE 10.5-11.5%) gives Rs220-330/sh, structurally lower because 24.9%-of-sales working capital and capex at 1.8x D&A mean only ~70% of profit converts to owner cash. Intersecting them, with the justified-P/B cross-check (Rs204-311) tugging toward the low end, I would defend Rs255-350 with a central value near Rs300. At Rs569.65 the market pays 42x earnings, 31x EV/EBITDA and a 1.66% FCF yield — a reverse-DCF says that requires ~13% FCF growth for a decade then 6% forever, which is an outcome to hope for, not a margin of safety; the price sits ~63% above my high end.

EXIDEIND.method_1: Sum-of-parts on NORMALISED CORE EARNINGS: core lead-acid PAT of ~Rs 950-1,050 cr (reported consolidated PAT 860 cr plus ~150 cr after-tax drag from the pre-revenue lithium-ion subsidiary) at a justified P/E of 13-18x. The multiple is derived, not borrowed: core equity ex-investments and ex-lithium-plant is only ~Rs 4,600 cr, so core ROE is ~22%; with g of 5-7% and CoE of 11-12.5%, the RI/DDM-justified P/E is 11.9x-18.2x. Core = Rs 12,350-18,900 cr; plus net financial assets of Rs 4,900-5,400 cr (non-current investments 5,300 + ST investments 831 + cash 1,082 - borrowings 1,575, haircut for tax leakage on the listed-equity stake); plus the lithium venture at 0.75-1.25x the ~Rs 3,960 cr of PPE built FY23-26 = Rs 3,000-5,000 cr. Total Rs 20,250-29,300 cr = Rs 237-342/share.
EXIDEIND.method_2: OWNER CASH FLOW: normalised core operating cash flow less maintenance capex, capitalised. Core EBITDA ~Rs 2,057 cr (1,882 reported plus ~175 lithium drag) less cash interest ~50, cash tax ~505 (31.1% effective on core EBIT) and ~100 of working-capital absorption gives normalised core OCF ~Rs 1,400 cr. Maintenance capex of Rs 500-650 cr (versus core depreciation of ~420 cr, reflecting a gross block of 11,829 cr and inventory+receivables at 31.7% of sales) leaves core owner earnings of Rs 750-900 cr. Capitalised at 13.3-16.7x (Gordon: CoE 11-12.5%, g 5-6%) gives core Rs 10,000-14,500 cr. Adding the same non-core assets gives Rs 17,900-24,900 cr = Rs 209-291/share.
EXIDEIND.methods_are_independent: Yes. Leg 1 is an accrual-earnings multiple; Leg 2 is a cash measure that never touches PAT and is anchored on maintenance capex and working capital, both of which are judgements independent of the income statement. They can and do diverge for this business specifically: over FY23-26 Exide earned cumulative PAT of Rs 3,366 cr but generated cumulative FCF of Rs +12 cr on OCF of 5,986 cr against capex of 5,973 cr. Even after stripping growth capex, the cash leg lands ~20% below the earnings leg because maintenance capex (~500-650 cr) exceeds core depreciation (~420 cr) and working capital at 31.7% of sales absorbs cash as revenue grows, while the earnings leg is depressed in the opposite direction by depreciation on a lithium plant that earns nothing yet. The legs also respond to different errors: Leg 1 breaks if my justified-P/E inputs (ROE, CoE) are wrong, Leg 2 breaks if maintenance capex is wrong.
